topics.title: Understanding pattern play

topics.title: Progressive difficulty benchmark
topics.narration: Open More for Sharivari’s progressive difficulty drill and use the demonstrated setup. Save the starting layout and record your first score. For your Trainer adaptation, begin with a comfortable position zone. After a successful set, reduce the zone or increase the shot difficulty, changing one condition at a time. Count both the pocketed ball and the required cue ball position. If the same error repeats, return to the last successful level. Record the highest level you can repeat, rather than only your best isolated attempt.

topics.title: 105-minute practice session
topics.narration: Use this one hundred and five minute practice plan. Spend thirty minutes on speed and target landing, aiming for eight successful pocket and position results out of ten with a three inch target. Spend forty five minutes on Rock Around the Clock, first completing one rotation and then working toward three consecutive rotations without disturbing another ball. Spend thirty minutes on kick escapes, starting with one rail and adding two and three rails as control improves. Test five selected escapes and aim for four legal contacts. Record the result at the end of each phase. If time runs out, save your layout and score, then continue there next session.

Watch his demonstration before practicing, and compare your expected landing point with the result. Open More for Zero X’s official lessons.

topics.title: Stop Shot Calibration
topics.narration: Stop Shot Calibration. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot end. Place the 1-ball on the center spot. Put the cue ball on the head string, one diamond from the left long rail. This lines up with the foot-right corner pocket. Center a three-inch white circle one ball width behind the 1-ball, toward the cue ball. That is the cue ball’s stopping position. Use no side spin. Start slightly below center and adjust your speed and tip height until the cue ball arrives without forward or backward roll. Pocket the 1-ball and stop the cue ball inside the white circle. Reset both balls after each attempt. Try five shots and count clean stops. In the Trainer, select Execute Shot to watch the result.

topics.title: 90-Degree Stun Tangent Line
topics.narration: Ninety-Degree Stun Tangent Line. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot. Place the 1-ball one diamond inward from the right side pocket. Put the cue ball on the table’s center line, half a diamond toward the foot end from the center spot. Place a three-inch yellow square one and a half diamonds toward the head end from the 1-ball, and one ball width to its left. Pocket the 1-ball into the right side pocket. Use no side spin and enough low tip contact and speed for the cue ball to be sliding at impact. It should leave along the tangent line, perpendicular to the object ball’s path. Adjust speed to finish inside the yellow square. Reset both balls and repeat five times. Select Execute Shot in the Trainer to compare the path with the tangent line.

topics.title: Speed Ladder — Four Zones
topics.narration: Speed Ladder. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot. Use only the cue ball. Start on the center line, half a diamond behind the head string. Place four three-inch circles on the center line: white on the center spot, red on the foot spot, yellow one diamond from the foot cushion, and pink one diamond from the head cushion. Reset the cue ball to the same starting position before every shot. First, stop on white. Second, stop on red. Third, touch the foot cushion and return to yellow. Fourth, touch the foot cushion and return all the way to pink. Use a level cue and no side spin. Change your stroke speed while keeping your delivery smooth. Score one point for each finish inside its circle, for a maximum of four. Repeat the ladder and compare your scores.

topics.title: L-Drill — Five-Ball Rotation
topics.narration: The L-Drill. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot. Place balls one, two, and three half a diamond from the right long rail, respectively one, two, and three diamonds from the foot cushion. Place ball four one diamond from the right long rail and half a diamond from the foot cushion. Place ball five on the center line, also half a diamond from the foot cushion. These five balls form an L. Put a white square at the center spot, one diamond wide. Start the cue ball on the center line, half a diamond behind the head string. Pocket balls one through five in order, choosing clear corner pockets. Plan the next angle before every shot. Use the center square as a recovery option when it helps the next shot. Count balls pocketed in sequence, then reset the full pattern and try again.

topics.title: T-Drill — Center and Foot String
topics.narration: The T-Drill. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot. Place ball one on the center spot. Place ball two one diamond farther toward the foot, and ball three on the foot spot. Put ball four on the foot string, one diamond to the left of ball three, and ball five one diamond to its right. Start the cue ball on the head string, one diamond from the right long rail. Place two yellow circles, each half a diamond wide, halfway between the center spot and the side pockets. Pocket balls one through five in order into corner pockets. Choose the yellow zone that gives you a useful angle for the next ball. Use a cushion when it helps the route. Keep the cue ball clear of the remaining balls. Count your run, reset the full pattern, and work toward completing all five.

topics.title: Wagon Wheel — Six Target Zones
topics.narration: The Wagon Wheel. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot. Place the 1-ball one diamond inward from the right side pocket. Put the cue ball on the center line, half a diamond toward the foot from the center spot. Set six three-inch circles on the head side of the 1-ball. Marker one is one and a half diamonds from the left rail and three and a half from the head rail. Marker two is two from the left and three from the head. Marker three is one ball width left of the 1-ball’s line and three from the head. Marker four is three and a quarter from the left and three from the head. Marker five is three and a half from the left and two and a half from the head. Marker six is directly headward of marker three, one and a half diamonds from the head rail. Reset both balls before every attempt and pocket the 1-ball into the right side pocket. Work through the markers in order, varying draw, follow, and speed. Start without side spin. Record the combinations that produce repeatable finishes.

topics.title: Two-Rail Center Recovery
topics.narration: Two-Rail Center Recovery. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot. Place the 1-ball one diamond from the right long rail and one diamond from the foot cushion. Put the cue ball on the same rail offset, three diamonds from the foot cushion. Place a white square on the center line, one diamond from the head cushion. Make the square one diamond wide. Pocket the 1-ball into the foot-right corner. Start with natural forward roll and no side spin. Look for the cue ball to contact the foot cushion, then the left long cushion, and travel toward the white recovery zone. Adjust your stroke speed to finish in the square. Keep the ball placements fixed so you can compare attempts. Score the pocketed ball and the position result separately. Try five shots, then repeat your most successful speed.

topics.title: Side Pocket Scratch Avoidance
topics.narration: Side Pocket Scratch Avoidance. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot. Place the 1-ball half a diamond inward from the right side pocket. Start the cue ball on the foot spot. Place a red square beside the head-right corner pocket, centered a quarter diamond from each cushion. Make it half a diamond wide. Place a white square on the center line, one diamond from the foot cushion, and make it one diamond wide. Pocket the 1-ball into the right side pocket. Compare forward roll, stun, and controlled draw, starting without side spin. Watch the whole cue ball route, including any cushion rebounds. Find a stroke that keeps the cue ball clear of the red danger zone and returns it toward white. In the Trainer, judge whether the path enters the red zone, even if cue ball pocketing is prevented. Reset both balls and repeat five times.

topics.title: One-Rail Mirror Kick
topics.narration: One-Rail Mirror Kick. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot. Put the cue ball on the head string, one diamond from the right long rail. Place the 1-ball on that same line, three diamonds from the foot cushion. Put the 8-ball halfway between them to block the direct shot. The cue ball and the 1-ball are now equally distant from the left cushion. Mark the left cushion halfway between their lengthwise positions: three and a half diamonds from the head cushion. Center a yellow circle one ball radius inside that cushion as the cue ball contact reference. Use a level cue, moderate speed, and no side spin. Send the cue ball to the left cushion, then into the 1-ball without touching the 8-ball first. Begin with the midpoint reference and make small aiming adjustments from your observed results. Reset the cue ball after each attempt and count five clean contacts.

topics.title: Two-Rail Corner Kick
topics.narration: Two-Rail Corner Kick. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot. Place the cue ball one diamond from the head cushion and one and a quarter diamonds from the right long rail. Put the 1-ball one diamond from the foot cushion and three quarters of a diamond from the right long rail. Place the 8-ball level with the side pockets, one diamond from the right rail. Put balls two and three on the same line, two ball widths to either side of the 8-ball toward the head and foot ends. This blocks the direct shot. Place yellow marker A at the right cushion on the foot string, with its center one ball radius inside the cloth. Place yellow marker B half a diamond left of the foot-right corner, also one ball radius inside the foot cushion. Use moderate speed and no side spin. Aim the cue ball center toward A. Look for right cushion, then foot cushion near B, then contact with the 1-ball. Make small aiming adjustments and count five successful escapes.

topics.title: Cue / Shaft Preset
topics.narration: Cue and Shaft Preset is in Advanced Physics and Calibration. Standard shaft keeps the original squirt setting. Low-deflection shaft reduces squirt while keeping the same tip spin. Custom opens the cue ball to end-mass ratio for individual adjustment. The choice applies to both shots and is saved with your settings.

topics.title: A repeatable pre-shot routine
topics.narration: While standing, choose pocket, route, and finish. Approach along the aim line, form a comfortable stance and bridge, rehearse smoothly, pause as needed, and deliver. Stand up and restart if the plan changes. Use the straight-shot layout. Have a partner observe or record video, then review consistency of the routine rather than copying a prescribed body shape.

topics.title: Comfortable stance and cue clearance
topics.narration: Plan while standing. Approach the shot, place your feet comfortably, and check that your body stays steady and the cue can move freely. Rise and realign if needed. Recreate the straight shot and observe from side/front video or with a coach. Adapt stance to your body; no single foot position is required.

topics.title: A stable bridge
topics.narration: Form a comfortable open or closed bridge on clear cloth. Rehearse slowly and check the hand remains still while the cue moves freely. Keep the bridge distance comfortable and consistent. Practice at the physical table with a coach, partner, or video. The on-screen cue does not model hand support or bridge stability.

topics.title: Reach, rail bridges, and cue access
topics.narration: Compare a clear-cloth cue-ball start with a rail-adjacent start. Identify bridge support, cue clearance, reach, and elevation before choosing the stroke. Inspect the actual cue approach and use a mechanical bridge when needed. Do not stretch into an unstable stroke; compare a simpler accessible route.
